audit: Sprint A1 — Parkio Complete Technical, Security and Production Audit

findings.title: No account deletion or data-erasure capability anywhere in the stack
findings.evidence: grep for account deletion/erasure across services and frontends returns no user-facing or admin flow; only DELETE endpoints are media soft-delete and notification device-token removal.
findings.description: There is no endpoint, admin tool, script, or documented operator procedure to delete a user account or erase a user's personal data (auth record, profile, refresh tokens, spots, media, logs, gamification, notifications).
findings.why_it_matters: GDPR/KVKK grant data subjects an erasure right. Once external testers register real accounts, the platform cannot honor deletion requests without ad-hoc SQL surgery across 9 databases plus MinIO.
findings.failure_scenario: An external beta tester emails a deletion request; the operator has no supported path and either ignores it (compliance exposure) or hand-edits 9 databases (integrity risk).
findings.hosted_beta_impact: Acceptable only for closed beta with informed internal testers; a written manual erasure runbook is the minimum stopgap.
findings.public_production_impact: Blocks public beta/production. Erasure must exist as a designed, event-driven cross-service flow before real users are onboarded.
findings.remediation: Design an account-deletion saga (auth-service originates a UserDeletionRequested event; each service erases/anonymizes its slice; media purges MinIO objects), plus a documented manual runbook as interim.
findings.validation_criteria: A deleted user's PII is verifiably absent from all 9 service databases, MinIO, and Redis after the flow completes; integration test proves it.

findings.title: Uncommitted landing/waitlist rework failed its own unit test at audit snapshot (fixed later the same day, still uncommitted)
findings.evidence: At the audit evidence snapshot (2026-07-12 ~16:30): 'LandingPage > submits the real waitlist flow successfully' timed out at the 5s test budget, reproduced deterministically in isolation. Re-checked at ~22:00 after the maintainer continued working on the tree: the file now passes 7/7. The fix remains uncommitted, and the previously packaged parkio-hostinger-landing.zip predates it. Original mechanism: waitFor timeout raised to 10s exceeded the 5s per-test budget; submit path lazy-imports waitlistService inside the handler.
findings.description: Working-tree (uncommitted) changes split waitlist constants into waitlistShared.ts, dynamic-import the API call at submit time, add a VITE_WAITLIST_INTAKE_MODE=disabled static mode, and add /privacy + /terms standalone bootstrapping. The happy-path waitlist submit test now fails deterministically. parkio-hostinger-landing.zip and dist/ were built from this tree.
findings.why_it_matters: The landing artifact just packaged for Hostinger deployment carries an unverified waitlist submit path; the suite is red so CI would reject this work.
findings.failure_scenario: If the dynamic import chain fails or stalls in the deployed bundle, a visitor clicks 'Join beta waitlist' and the form spins forever; the signup is silently lost.
findings.hosted_beta_impact: Landing page deploys should wait until the suite is green or intake mode is 'disabled' (static mode renders without the submit path).
findings.public_production_impact: Same as beta; also erodes trust in the test gate if committed red.
findings.remediation: Commit the fix, re-run the FULL web suite green, and rebuild parkio-hostinger-landing.zip from the fixed tree before deploying; verify one live submit against a running gateway.
findings.validation_criteria: corepack pnpm --filter @parkio/web test passes on the committed tree; the deployed artifact is rebuilt from that commit; a manual submit records 202.

findings.title: Single-node data plane: no HA Postgres/PITR, single Kafka broker, single MinIO
findings.evidence: docker-compose.yml / hosted-beta overlay run 9 Postgres containers, 1 Kafka (KRaft, RF=1 default via parkio.kafka.replication-factor), 1 MinIO, 1 Redis on one host; docs/architecture/production-readiness.md and KNOWN-ISSUES HB-02/PP-01..03 state this openly.
findings.description: The entire data plane lives on one VPS with volume-level backups (scripted daily dumps) but no PITR, no replication, no failover.
findings.why_it_matters: Host loss means full outage; disk loss means losing everything since the last backup window.
findings.failure_scenario: VPS dies at 23:00; nightly backup was 01:00; the beta loses a day of spots, verifications, waitlist entries; recovery is manual restore (hours).
findings.hosted_beta_impact: Acceptable, documented risk for a closed invite beta with backup runbook discipline.
findings.public_production_impact: Blocks public production (matches the repo's own NO-GO). Requires managed Postgres with PITR, Kafka RF>=3 or managed alternative, S3/versioned media storage.
findings.remediation: For beta: enforce backup schedule + weekly restore drill on the real host, monitor disk. For production: execute the managed-services migration already planned in production-readiness.md.
findings.validation_criteria: Documented RPO/RTO met in a live restore drill; production migration validated in staging.

findings.title: No open-source license selected; repository is source-visible only
findings.evidence: LICENSE file explicitly reserves all rights pending maintainer license selection; README and KNOWN-ISSUES OSS-01 repeat it.
findings.description: A deliberate 'license pending' placeholder blocks any public open-source distribution and makes external contribution legally ambiguous.
findings.why_it_matters: Public repo promotion, contributions, or reuse before selection creates legal ambiguity for everyone involved.
findings.failure_scenario: A contributor forks and builds on the code assuming OSS; rights are unclear; dispute risk.
findings.hosted_beta_impact: No impact on hosted beta (operator-run).
findings.public_production_impact: Blocks open-source publication (repo already says NO GO).
findings.remediation: Maintainer/legal decision: pick a license, replace LICENSE, add NOTICE if required, update README/SECURITY/release docs. Not chosen by this audit per instructions.
findings.validation_criteria: LICENSE contains final text; README/SECURITY updated; NOTICE added if the license requires it.

findings.title: Edge rate limiting likely fails open when Redis is down (framework default)
findings.evidence: All gateway routes use Spring Cloud Gateway RequestRateLimiter with RedisRateLimiter (application.yml routes; RateLimitConfig key resolver). Stock RedisRateLimiter treats Redis errors as 'allow' — no override or custom error handling exists in gateway code.
findings.description: Spring Cloud Gateway's built-in Redis token bucket allows requests through when the Redis call fails. Parkio does not customize this, so a Redis outage silently removes brute-force and abuse throttling at the edge (auth-service's own Redis-backed login lockout would also be down, see SEC-002).
findings.why_it_matters: The credential-stuffing and enumeration defense on /auth/login evaporates exactly during a Redis incident.
findings.failure_scenario: Attacker (or bad luck) coincides with Redis outage; login endpoint accepts unthrottled credential-stuffing traffic while the account-lockout tracker is equally unavailable.
findings.hosted_beta_impact: Moderate: closed beta has few accounts; still worth an alert on redis_up.
findings.public_production_impact: For production, decide the posture explicitly (fail-open with alerting vs fail-closed on auth routes) and test it.
findings.remediation: Verify behavior with Redis stopped (chaos test exists in repo scaffolding); add an Alertmanager rule on Redis down; consider a deny-fallback for /auth/** routes.
findings.validation_criteria: Chaos run with Redis stopped shows the chosen posture and pages the operator.

findings.title: Redis is an availability single point of failure for login and waitlist
findings.evidence: RedisLoginFailureTracker and RedisWaitlistRateLimiter propagate Redis exceptions (no fallback/catch); login and waitlist requests error out when Redis is unreachable.
findings.description: Security-relevant limiters correctly fail closed, but that makes a Redis outage a full login outage (fail-closed is the safer default; the trade-off is availability).
findings.why_it_matters: Single Redis container down -> no user can log in, no waitlist signup succeeds, and gateway session-epoch/user-status caches also degrade.
findings.failure_scenario: Redis OOM or restart during beta demo; every login 500s until Redis returns.
findings.hosted_beta_impact: Acceptable if monitored; operators must know Redis is on the critical path.
findings.public_production_impact: Production needs managed/HA Redis or an explicit degraded-mode decision.
findings.remediation: Document the posture; alert on Redis health; consider bounded in-memory fallback only if the posture decision calls for it.
findings.validation_criteria: Runbook documents Redis-down behavior; alert fires in chaos drill.

findings.title: Per-user location behavior logs grow forever (search + view logs, no retention)
findings.evidence: parking_spot_search_logs stores searcher_user_id + exact lat/lng + radius per search; parking_spot_view_logs stores viewer_user_id per spot view. The parking RetentionCleanupJob deletes only outbox/inbox rows.
findings.description: Fine-grained user movement/interest data accumulates indefinitely with no retention policy, no aggregation, and no deletion path — while the project's stated principle is location minimization.
findings.why_it_matters: Contradicts the privacy posture claimed in README/startup docs; grows into a sensitive dataset and a liability; also unbounded table growth.
findings.failure_scenario: A year of beta produces a precise history of where each user searched for parking; a breach or subpoena exposes movement patterns.
findings.hosted_beta_impact: Low volume in closed beta, but the policy gap should be closed before external users.
findings.public_production_impact: Public launch with indefinite raw location logs invites regulatory and reputational risk.
findings.remediation: Add a retention window (e.g. 90 days) to the existing RetentionCleanupJob pattern, or aggregate to daily counts and drop raw rows; document it on the privacy page.
findings.validation_criteria: Rows older than the window are provably deleted by the scheduled job; privacy page states the window.

findings.title: Legal privacy/terms pages are explicit placeholders; waitlist has no deletion/retention procedure
findings.evidence: LegalPage.tsx labels both pages 'hosted-beta placeholder'; waitlist_interest stores raw email with consent_timestamp but no retention or deletion mechanism exists.
findings.description: The public site collects email PII (waitlist) under placeholder legal text, and there is no way to honor a waitlist removal request except manual SQL.
findings.why_it_matters: Collecting real emails under placeholder terms is a compliance and trust problem the moment collection opens to the public.
findings.failure_scenario: A signee requests removal citing KVKK; there is no endpoint, admin surface, or runbook for it.
findings.hosted_beta_impact: Real waitlist collection should not open until minimally accurate legal text exists and a deletion procedure (even a documented SQL runbook) is in place.
findings.public_production_impact: Blocks public launch; final legal review is explicitly out of scope for engineering docs.
findings.remediation: Have counsel (or founder with template review) finalize beta-scope privacy/terms; add a waitlist-removal runbook or admin endpoint; define waitlist retention.
findings.validation_criteria: Legal pages no longer say placeholder; a removal request can be executed and evidenced.

findings.title: Mobile device runtime smoke never executed for the release line; store-readiness blockers open
findings.evidence: KNOWN-ISSUES HB-01 and FINAL-FRONTEND-CERTIFICATION state device smoke was not run for FFINAL (emulator present, dev-client session not recorded); play-store listing artwork/owner blockers tracked in docs/beta/.
findings.description: The Expo app has strong unit coverage (SecureStore tokens, refresh flow, RBAC parity) but no recorded login+upload smoke on a physical device for the RC.
findings.why_it_matters: Mobile-specific runtime failures (push, camera, secure store on real hardware) would surface first on testers' phones.
findings.failure_scenario: A beta tester installs the preview APK; camera capture or push registration fails in a way emulators/unit tests did not exercise.
findings.hosted_beta_impact: Run the documented device smoke before widening mobile beta (repo's own caveat).
findings.public_production_impact: Store submission additionally blocked on artwork/account ownership tasks.
findings.remediation: Execute docs/beta/mobile-release.md smoke on a physical device and record evidence; close listing blockers.
findings.validation_criteria: Recorded device smoke: login, spot create with camera photo, push receipt, logout.

findings.title: GitHub Actions are tag-pinned, not commit-SHA-pinned
findings.evidence: All workflows reference actions like actions/checkout@v4, github/codeql-action@v4, docker/login-action@v3 by mutable tag.
findings.description: A compromised or force-moved action tag executes attacker code in CI with access to workflow permissions (mostly contents:read, but release jobs hold packages:write/id-token:write).
findings.why_it_matters: Tag-pinning is the main residual CI supply-chain exposure in an otherwise disciplined setup (least-privilege permissions, gitleaks, Trivy, SBOMs, draft-gated publish).
findings.failure_scenario: Upstream action tag is retargeted maliciously; next release workflow run exfiltrates the GHCR token or poisons images.
findings.hosted_beta_impact: Low direct beta impact; images are built from these pipelines.
findings.public_production_impact: Production-grade supply chain expects SHA pinning plus Dependabot actions updates.
findings.remediation: Pin every third-party action to a full commit SHA (Dependabot keeps them fresh); one PR.
findings.validation_criteria: grep 'uses:' shows only sha-pinned refs; Dependabot config covers github-actions ecosystem.

findings.title: Ten-service microservice topology is heavy for a pre-user product
findings.evidence: 10 Spring Boot JVMs + gateway + 9 Postgres + Kafka + Redis + MinIO + ClamAV + observability. Measured idle footprint ~7.7 GiB (benchmarks/reports/p221). Recommended host 8 vCPU/24 GB (runtime-sizing.md).
findings.description: Service boundaries are clean (db-per-service, events, no shared domain), but the fixed operational cost — memory, deploy surface, 9 schemas to migrate/backup, 15 CI workflows — is large relative to zero users.
findings.why_it_matters: Every operational task (backup, upgrade, incident) is multiplied by ~10; VPS cost floor is high; onboarding cost is high.
findings.failure_scenario: A solo operator burns beta time nursing 25+ containers instead of shipping product.
findings.hosted_beta_impact: Runs, but leaves little headroom on affordable VPS tiers; sizing doc is honest about this.
findings.public_production_impact: For production the topology is defensible only with managed data services; consolidation of low-traffic services (analytics+ai-validation+gamification) is the documented cheaper path.
findings.remediation: No action now (repo already documents consolidation candidates); revisit after beta metrics.
findings.validation_criteria: Decision record after beta: consolidate or keep, with load data attached.

findings.title: Infrastructure plumbing is copy-pasted across all services by design; drift risk
findings.evidence: OutboxRelay, RetentionCleanupJob, GatewayAuthFilter, CorrelationIdFilter, inbox adapters are near-identical in 9 services (auth vs media OutboxRelay differ by ~52 diff lines, mostly renames). platform/parkio-platform holds only 7 shared transport/tracing classes.
findings.description: settings.gradle.kts documents 'no shared domain modules on purpose'. Domain isolation is correct, but transport-level plumbing duplication means a bug fix (e.g. the SEC-001 posture, a DLQ edge case) must be applied nine times.
findings.why_it_matters: Nine chances to miss a fix; slow security patching; review fatigue.
findings.failure_scenario: A poison-message handling fix lands in 7 of 9 relays; the other two dead-letter differently and page the operator months later.
findings.hosted_beta_impact: Tolerable at current churn.
findings.public_production_impact: Growing team/production cadence will want the plumbing (not domain) promoted into parkio-platform.
findings.remediation: Move service-agnostic plumbing (relay skeleton, retention job, gateway-auth filter) into platform module while keeping event payloads/domain service-owned.
findings.validation_criteria: One implementation of each plumbing class; services configure, not copy.

findings.title: All Docker-dependent verification was BLOCKED in this audit environment
findings.evidence: Docker Desktop daemon unreachable from WSL session (docker.exe: cannot connect to //./pipe/docker_engine). integrationTest, docker compose config, real-stack Playwright, restore drill, chaos scripts all need it. CI runs these (backend-integration.yml with requireDocker=true, weekly backup-restore-drill.yml), but they were not re-executed locally by this audit.
findings.description: Unit-level evidence is fresh and green (712 backend tests re-executed; 293 web/api-client vitest). Integration/e2e/restore claims rest on CI history and certification docs, not on this audit's own runs.
findings.why_it_matters: The audit cannot independently confirm Kafka/Postgres/MinIO integration behavior or compose validity today.
findings.failure_scenario: A regression that only integration suites catch would be invisible to this audit.
findings.hosted_beta_impact: Start Docker Desktop and run: ./gradlew integrationTest -Pparkio.integrationTest.requireDocker=true; docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml -f docker/docker-compose.apps.yml config; scripts/validate-hosted-beta-compose.sh.
findings.public_production_impact: Same commands gate production claims.
findings.remediation: Re-run the blocked commands on a Docker-capable host and attach results to the test-evidence doc.
findings.validation_criteria: All listed commands recorded PASS on the audited commit.

findings.title: Write-path performance is unmeasured; read path has real evidence
findings.evidence: benchmarks/reports/p221 records a genuine multi-user read benchmark (1,182 req/s, p95 ~6 ms, 0 errors, never saturated) and states plainly that upload/spot-create writes were not exercised.
findings.description: Uploads traverse ClamAV scan + image re-encode + MinIO write + outbox; spot creation fans out Kafka events. None of this is load-tested.
findings.why_it_matters: The most expensive path (media) is exactly the untested one.
findings.failure_scenario: Beta announcement drives 50 concurrent uploads; ClamAV (1 GiB RAM, single container) becomes the bottleneck; uploads time out.
findings.hosted_beta_impact: Low concurrency expected in closed beta; media rate limit (2 rps replenish) caps exposure.
findings.public_production_impact: Public production requires a write-path load test with media in the mix (repo already lists this as a blocker, PP-06).
findings.remediation: Extend the k6 harness with an upload/spot-create scenario against a disposable stack; measure ClamAV throughput.
findings.validation_criteria: Recorded write-path benchmark with stated limits and headroom.

findings.title: Alert delivery, uptime monitoring and on-call are operator-TODO; alerts route to null by default
findings.evidence: alertmanager.yml default receiver is 'null' (render-config.sh injects a real webhook only if env is set); 42 Prometheus alert rules exist; no synthetic/uptime check of the public domain in repo; PP-05 documents on-call as partial.
findings.description: The observability stack is provisioned (Prometheus/Grafana/Loki/Tempo/Alertmanager, dashboards, blackbox exporter config), but out of the box nothing pages a human.
findings.why_it_matters: 42 well-formed alerts that reach no receiver equal zero alerts.
findings.failure_scenario: Cert renewal fails silently; beta domain serves an expired certificate for days until a tester complains.
findings.hosted_beta_impact: Wire the webhook (env) and an external uptime ping before inviting testers.
findings.public_production_impact: Production needs a real on-call rota and escalation.
findings.remediation: Set PARKIO_ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL at deploy (preflight could enforce non-empty for hosted-beta), add a free external uptime monitor for the three domains.
findings.validation_criteria: Test alert reaches the operator's channel; uptime monitor alarms on synthetic downtime.

findings.title: Developer machine npm configuration disables TLS to the package registry
findings.evidence: ~/.npmrc (user home, not the repo) sets registry=http://registry.npmjs.org/ and strict-ssl=false; observed when pnpm audit hit the registry over HTTP (426 response).
findings.description: Package metadata and any dependency resolution outside the lockfile happen over plaintext HTTP on this machine. Lockfile sha512 integrity pins existing deps, but new/updated dependency resolution is exposed to tampering.
findings.why_it_matters: The repo's lockfile discipline is undermined at the workstation that produces the lockfile.
findings.failure_scenario: On-path attacker on the dev network serves a poisoned tarball for a newly added package; its hash lands in the committed lockfile.
findings.hosted_beta_impact: Not a repo defect; fix the workstation.
findings.public_production_impact: Same.
findings.remediation: Delete the registry/strict-ssl lines from ~/.npmrc (defaults are HTTPS + strict TLS).
findings.validation_criteria: pnpm config get registry returns https://registry.npmjs.org/; strict-ssl true.

findings.title: Alertmanager placeholder receiver ships by default (see OPS-001) and infra/ IaC is a stub
findings.evidence: infra/ contains only README/CLAUDE placeholders (HB-03 documents this); deployment is compose + operator scripts by design for beta.
findings.description: No Terraform/Kubernetes automation exists; the hosted beta path is deliberately script-driven.
findings.why_it_matters: Environment rebuilds are manual and rely on runbook fidelity.
findings.failure_scenario: VPS must be rebuilt; operator follows HOSTED-BETA-RUNBOOK.md by hand; drift possible.
findings.hosted_beta_impact: Fine for one host.
findings.public_production_impact: Production/AWS needs at least minimal IaC for the network/data tier.
findings.remediation: Defer until AWS phase; then Terraform the VPC/RDS/ECS skeleton.
findings.validation_criteria: Environment reproducible from code.

findings.title: Local dev docker/.env holds a real RSA private key in plaintext (gitignored, untracked)
findings.evidence: docker/.env (verified untracked and ignored via .gitignore:35, git ls-files empty) contains a full PKCS#8 private key and local-dev passwords. Committed *.env.example files hold only CHANGE_ME placeholders; gitleaks + push protection + preflight CHANGE_ME checks guard the repo boundary.
findings.description: Standard local-dev practice, but the key doubles as the dev JWT signing key; any process/user on the workstation can read it.
findings.why_it_matters: If this dev key were ever reused in a hosted environment, its exposure would be an auth compromise; runbooks already forbid reuse (OP-03).
findings.failure_scenario: Dev machine malware exfiltrates the key; harmless only as long as it never signs non-local tokens.
findings.hosted_beta_impact: None if key stays local-only.
findings.public_production_impact: None if rotation discipline holds.
findings.remediation: Keep dev keys clearly labeled, never reuse in hosted envs (already documented); optionally move hosted-beta secrets to an encrypted store on the VPS.
findings.validation_criteria: Hosted env uses a freshly generated key (preflight already enforces non-placeholder).

findings.title: Container base images are tag-pinned, not digest-pinned
findings.evidence: Dockerfiles use eclipse-temurin:21-jdk/-jre, node:22-bookworm-slim, nginx:1.27-alpine by tag.
findings.description: Tags are mutable; a rebuild can silently pull different base content. Trivy scanning mitigates known-CVE risk but not substitution.
findings.why_it_matters: Two builds of the same commit may not be identical at the base layer despite the reproducible-jar work.
findings.failure_scenario: Registry-side tag repoint changes the runtime base under a hotfix rebuild.
findings.hosted_beta_impact: Minor for beta.
findings.public_production_impact: Digest-pin plus automated digest bumps is the production norm.
findings.remediation: Pin FROM lines to sha256 digests; let Dependabot/Renovate bump them.
findings.validation_criteria: All FROM lines carry digests; CI green.

findings.title: One moderate npm advisory: transitive uuid <11.1.1 via Expo xcode tooling
findings.evidence: pnpm audit --prod (HTTPS): 1 moderate (GHSA-w5hq-g745-h8pq), 281 paths, all under @expo/cli config-plugins > xcode > uuid@7.0.3 — build-time tooling, not shipped app code.
findings.description: Vulnerable uuid is used by Expo's Xcode project generator during prebuild, not in the runtime bundle.
findings.why_it_matters: Negligible runtime exposure; hygiene item.
findings.failure_scenario: None realistic.
findings.hosted_beta_impact: None.
findings.public_production_impact: None.
findings.remediation: Track Expo SDK updates; add a pnpm audit gate to frontend CI if desired.
findings.validation_criteria: pnpm audit --prod reports 0 known vulnerabilities.

findings.title: Notification NEARBY_PARKING fan-out is a TODO (documented accepted risk AR-01)
findings.evidence: Single TODO in main code: NotificationApplicationService:92 — nearby-user fan-out not implemented; inbox/push per-user paths work.
findings.description: A documented product gap, not a defect: nearby drivers are not notified of new spots.
findings.why_it_matters: Feature value gap in beta; core notification plumbing unaffected.
findings.failure_scenario: Users expect nearby alerts (marketing copy mentions freshness); they never arrive.
findings.hosted_beta_impact: Set expectations in beta comms.
findings.public_production_impact: Implement before marketing the feature.
findings.remediation: Implement geo-fanout (parking event -> user-service nearby query -> notification), respecting privacy minimization.
findings.validation_criteria: Nearby user receives push in integration test.

findings.title: Analytics snapshot reads are unbounded findAll() (slow-growing tables)
findings.evidence: AnalyticsApplicationService returns dailySnapshots.findAll()/parkingSnapshots.findAll() with no pagination; tables grow ~1 row/day/dimension.
findings.description: Years of operation would make admin analytics responses large; not a beta problem.
findings.why_it_matters: Slow admin dashboard someday.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin endpoint returns multi-MB payload after years.
findings.hosted_beta_impact: None.
findings.public_production_impact: Minor.
findings.remediation: Add date-range parameters (already natural for snapshots).
findings.validation_criteria: Endpoints accept from/to and default to a bounded window.

findings.title: No database CHECK constraints on latitude/longitude ranges
findings.evidence: parking_spots migration defines lat/lng DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL without range CHECKs; validation happens in application code only.
findings.description: Schema admits lat=999; the PostGIS trigger would compute a garbage geography point rather than reject it.
findings.why_it_matters: Defense-in-depth gap; bad data via any non-API write path (manual fix, future bug) persists silently.
findings.failure_scenario: A buggy backfill writes swapped lat/lng; nearby search silently misses those spots.
findings.hosted_beta_impact: Negligible.
findings.public_production_impact: Cheap hardening.
findings.remediation: Add CHECK (latitude BETWEEN -90 AND 90) and (longitude BETWEEN -180 AND 180) in a new migration.
findings.validation_criteria: Constraint present; insert of out-of-range values fails.

findings.title: Five ESLint warnings in the web app (react-refresh export patterns)
findings.evidence: pnpm -r lint exits 0 with 5 warnings in apps/web (react-refresh/only-export-components).
findings.description: Cosmetic; affects HMR ergonomics only.
findings.why_it_matters: None.
findings.failure_scenario: None.
findings.hosted_beta_impact: None.
findings.public_production_impact: None.
findings.remediation: Split mixed component/constant exports or accept and silence with rationale.
findings.validation_criteria: Lint reports 0 warnings.

findings.title: KNOWN-ISSUES OP-06 ('backup restore not automated in CI') is stale — a weekly CI restore drill exists
findings.evidence: backup-restore-drill.yml runs weekly (cron 23 4 * * 1) restoring real dumps against real migrations; OP-06 still claims restore is not automated.
findings.description: Documentation understates the project here (rare direction). CI drill covers script correctness, not the live host's volumes — that nuance belongs in the doc.
findings.why_it_matters: Operators may skip a drill that exists, or over-trust CI coverage of their specific host.
findings.failure_scenario: Confusion during incident about what restore evidence exists.
findings.hosted_beta_impact: Update the row to distinguish CI drill (exists) from live-host drill (operator duty).
findings.public_production_impact: None.
findings.remediation: Doc fix.
findings.validation_criteria: KNOWN-ISSUES row reflects the workflow accurately.

findings.title: Waitlist HMAC hash secret defaults to reusing the gateway internal secret
findings.evidence: application.yml: parkio.waitlist.hash-secret defaults to ${PARKIO_GATEWAY_INTERNAL_SECRET:} when PARKIO_WAITLIST_HASH_SECRET is unset.
findings.description: One secret serving two purposes (service-mesh auth + PII pseudonymization) couples their rotation and blast radius; otherwise the waitlist design (raw IP never stored, HMAC-SHA256, >=32-char enforcement) is good.
findings.why_it_matters: Rotating the gateway secret silently changes waitlist hashes, breaking dedupe/rate-limit continuity; leaking one secret weakens the other's purpose.
findings.failure_scenario: Gateway secret rotation day: every prior email_hash no longer matches, unique constraint lets duplicates in.
findings.hosted_beta_impact: Set both env vars distinctly (hosted-beta env example may already; verify at deploy).
findings.public_production_impact: Set distinct secrets everywhere.
findings.remediation: Require PARKIO_WAITLIST_HASH_SECRET explicitly in hosted profiles (preflight check).
findings.validation_criteria: Preflight fails when the two secrets are identical or waitlist secret unset.

findings.title: One flaky mobile test under slow I/O (SmartReturnScreen search flow)
findings.evidence: Full-suite jest --runInBand run failed 'searches, selects a home area, and saves the settings' (testID smartReturn.home.result.g1 not found, suite took 85.6s on WSL /mnt/c); the same file passes 10/10 in isolation (96s). Timing-sensitive async/debounce under constrained I/O.
findings.description: The test depends on async search results appearing within default timeouts, which slow environments miss during full-suite runs.
findings.why_it_matters: Flaky tests erode trust in the gate and train people to re-run red CI.
findings.failure_scenario: A legitimate Smart Return regression is dismissed as 'the flaky one'.
findings.hosted_beta_impact: None functional.
findings.public_production_impact: None functional.
findings.remediation: Raise the specific waitFor/test timeout or await the debounce deterministically (fake timers).
findings.validation_criteria: Full suite passes 3x consecutively in a constrained environment.

findings.title: Verified security strengths (recorded for due diligence)
findings.evidence: Code-verified: gateway strips inbound X-User-*/X-Gateway-Auth before stamping; RS256+JWKS with audience/issuer/skew enforcement; fail-closed user-status + session-epoch checks (503 on dependency loss); refresh tokens stored as SHA-256 of high-entropy values with family revocation and reuse detection bumping session epoch; BCrypt passwords; constant-time secret comparison (MessageDigest.isEqual) with rotation window support; Redis login lockout; media pipeline: content-type sniffing, pixel/size caps, EXIF handling with re-encode, ClamAV, private bucket + presigned SigV4 GETs; edge CSP/HSTS/Permissions-Policy at Caddy; actuator limited to health,info,prometheus; web access token memory-only + HttpOnly refresh cookie; SW never caches API/auth; mobile tokens in SecureStore with allowBackup=false; non-root containers with mem/cpu/pids limits and !reset ports in hosted overlay; CORS deny-by-default allow-list failing fast on wildcard+credentials.
findings.description: The security architecture matches its documentation at every point this audit sampled.
findings.why_it_matters: Positive finding: prior certification claims are substantiated.
findings.failure_scenario: n/a

findings.public_production_impact: n/a
